title: A femtosecond pulse spreads in glass
caption: A short pulse has a wide spectrum, and glass delays its colours by different amounts. A 20 fs pulse through 1 cm of glass (GDD = 360 fs²) leaves about 54 fs long: τ = τ₀√(1 + (4 ln 2 GDD/τ₀²)²). Shorter pulses broaden far more.
alt: Output pulse duration against group-delay dispersion, rising from 20 femtoseconds and becoming nearly a straight line, with 54 femtoseconds at 360 square femtoseconds marked.
description: Chirped mirrors or prism pairs add opposite GDD to undo it.
